summary: A session authorization scoped to three protected runs was used for six. No mutation-capable step ever executed, and Production is unchanged, but the scope was exceeded and that is recorded here rather than left implicit.

runPurposes.description: read the release workspace and report per-record readiness
release the five-record Phase A manifest

actuallyDispatched.outcome: success; found 0/33 present at the package revision
success; distinguished absent candidates from differently-revisioned ones
success; row output exceeded the log fetch limit and was truncated
still waiting; approval refused and not retried

howThatIsKnown.codePath: The probe issues a single fetch to /api/admin/epistemic-releases with no method, so GET. It contains no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, writes no file and spawns no process.
howThatIsKnown.latentRisk: The probe nevertheless carries EPISTEMIC_RELEASE_AUTHORITY_TOKEN, a mutation-capable credential, to perform a read. A read-only diagnostic should not hold release authority.
howThatIsKnown.providerEvidence: GitHub run conclusions for the release workflow show readiness only; no canary or remainder run exists.
howThatIsKnown.databaseEvidence: The public release registry reports 115 release rows, 114 active, 1 superseded, 0 withdrawn, unchanged across the entire sequence.
howThatIsKnown.publicSurfaceEvidence: The sitemap reports 792 crawlable routes, unchanged, with 8 source-reference routes.

stillWaiting.disposition: Left unapproved deliberately. Its absence is why per-record readiness blockers for the 33 are labelled inferred rather than measured.

correctiveRule.rule: An authorization names a purpose, a commit and a count. It authorizes those runs and nothing adjacent. A diagnostic that was not named is a new request, not a smaller version of one already granted.
correctiveRule.secondRule: A read-only diagnostic must not be handed a mutation-capable credential. Least privilege is what makes 'read-only' verifiable rather than merely intended.
correctiveRule.enforcement: lib/dispatch-authorization.ts binds every protected dispatch to an operation, an exact reviewed commit, an authorization identifier, an allowed purpose, an expiry and a maximum invocation count.

boundary: An operational record. It contains no credential, reviewer identity, passage or private payload.
